Q51.q: Many groups have recently started booking flights, and we are receiving many questions about whether accommodation can be requested from the 1st to the 10th. If possible, how do we apply?
Q51.a: The schedule differs depending on the type of package. There is no package that allows a stay from 1 to 10 August. Please note that A1 is 2–9 August, and A1+1 is divided into 1–9 August or 2–10 August.

Q52.q: On what basis are accommodation and the responsible parish allocated? We would also like to know whether we can choose an accommodation option or a specific parish when registering, or whether allocation is on a first-come, first-served basis.
Q52.a: Pilgrims cannot choose a specific type of accommodation or parish in advance; accommodation allocation is decided according to the overall operating situation and capacity. Accommodation is not allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. However, for groups that have completed both registration and payment, the information checks and procedures for allocation can proceed smoothly, so we recommend completing registration and payment as soon as possible.

Q53.q: We would like to know whether two different groups can be allocated to the same accommodation on request.
Q53.a: Please understand that it may be difficult to allocate different groups to the same accommodation. If you pass on this request to the Local Organising Committee after registering, we will do our best to help.

Q54.q: Our group has participants who speak English, French and Spanish. Will the group's participants be divided by language, or can they stay in the same accommodation?
Q54.a: As a rule, the same group is allocated to the same accommodation. If you wish to be allocated to the same accommodation, please register as the same group. However, depending on the operating situation and capacity, members of the same group may unavoidably be allocated to different accommodation. In this case, they will be allocated to accommodation as close together as possible.

Q55.q: Will homestay accommodation still be available after the event, or will we mostly stay in facilities such as churches or gyms? Because of transport constraints, we may have to split a group of 100 across two or three flights, in which case some will arrive before 2 August. What is the procedure in this case? Will they be accepted at the accommodation allocated to the group as it is?
Q55.a:
The dates of your stay are determined by the package you choose.
If you need accommodation on dates not included in your package, you must arrange it yourselves.

Q56.q: Where do we stay on the evening of Monday 2 August? Do we stay in the diocese, or are we already in Seoul?
Q56.a:
Your accommodation dates are determined by the schedule of the package you choose.
For example, the A1 package covers 2–9 August, so on 2 August you will stay at a location in Seoul.

Q57.q: Can pilgrims who need to rest during the day because of heatstroke, exhaustion or illness caused by a heatwave use their accommodation or a separate rest area? Also, can the accommodation be used after the closing Mass if necessary?
Q57.a:
During the main event, if you need to rest during the day because of a heatwave or health problems, you can use the hub parishes designated by the district committees in each district as rest areas. Pilgrims can go to these hub parishes to rest.
Also, if you have chosen a package that includes the option of staying after the closing Mass, you can use your accommodation.

Q58.q: Regarding packages, can our group take part without accommodation and transport? If so, how much does it cost? Most packages include transport, so we wonder whether there is an option without these services. Thank you.
Q58.a: Please understand that transport is included in all packages and cannot be excluded. There are packages without accommodation, so please use one of those.

Q59.q: Will meals on Saturday 7 August be provided as packed meals (meal boxes), or do we need to pay by card before going to the vigil venue?
Q59.a: In line with the meal composition of each package, meal boxes will be provided during the Vigil and the closing Mass. The meal boxes cover four meals in total: lunch and dinner on 7 August and breakfast and lunch on 8 August. Pilgrim packages that include meal boxes receive these four meals as meal boxes, without paying separately with the prepaid meal card. On-site arrangements such as the exact distribution times and locations will be announced later.

Q60.q: How will meal options be provided for pilgrims with special dietary needs such as food allergies, gluten intolerance or vegetarianism? Will information on allergens and ingredients such as peanuts, beef, seafood, shrimp and vegetarian options be available for the packed meals and at the outlets that accept the prepaid meal card? Also, must allergy information be registered only through the app, or are other methods available?
Q60.a: Regarding meals, we are reviewing whether to provide special meals such as gluten-free and vegan options and how to display food information. We are also reviewing whether and how food information such as allergens and ingredients will be provided at the outlets that accept the prepaid meal card. The scope of special meals, how to apply for them and the deadline for changes will be announced as soon as the detailed operating plan is confirmed.

Q61.q: Will special transport support (transport for people with disabilities or patients) be provided for people who are injured or ill during WYD?
Q61.a: Ambulances will be on standby around the event venues at all times, and we plan to provide medical services in cooperation with nearby hospitals.

Q62.q: According to the safeguarding policy, a minor in Korea is someone under 18 years and 7 months, but in our country it is someone under 18. In this case, there will be no chaperone letter.
Q62.a: The age of majority may differ by country, but for participation in WYD Seoul, the criteria of the 'Guidelines for the Protection of Minors and Vulnerable Adults' apply. These guidelines apply the age criterion of the Korean Youth Protection Act and classify participants born on or after 1 January 2009 as minors. This is also the criterion for roles that require adult status, such as pilgrim group leaders and deputy leaders, volunteers and chaperones of minors. Therefore, even participants who are recognised as adults in their own country must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian, or by an adult chaperone delegated by them, if they fall within the above date-of-birth criterion. At least one adult chaperone is required for every 10 minors. A delegated adult chaperone must obtain a written letter of delegation and consent from the minor's parent or legal guardian and carry it throughout the event.

Q63.q: How is the registration of minors carried out within a Macrogroup? Are minors registered first and chaperones afterwards, or are specific chaperones and minors registered together?
Q63.a: In step 2 of registration, you enter the total number of participants in the group and the number and gender of minors. Even within a Macrogroup, there is no set order for registering minors and chaperones, and there is no separate procedure for linking specific chaperones and minors in registration. However, under the WYD Seoul 'Guidelines for the Protection of Minors and Vulnerable Adults', at least one adult chaperone must accompany every 10 minors. A delegated adult chaperone must obtain a written letter of delegation and consent from the minor's parent or legal guardian and carry it throughout the event. In addition, when minors are allocated to a homestay, one adult chaperone of the same gender must accompany every two minors of the same gender. Therefore, please register minors and chaperones taking into account the number and gender composition of chaperones required by the above guidelines.

Q64.q: If a problem arises with a young person aged 18–19, does Korean law apply, or the law of the young person's home country?
Q64.a: Korean law applies by default, and depending on each country's legislation, the law of the home country may also apply.

Q65.q: Are special documents required for minor pilgrims to take part, such as consent from parents or legal representatives and the appointment of a chaperone? Will official forms (in Korean/English) be provided?
Q65.a: For a minor pilgrim to take part, a written consent is required in which the parent or legal guardian agrees to the minor's participation and entrusts the protection of the minor to an adult chaperone during the event. Under the Korean Youth Protection Act, the chaperone of a minor must be an adult (born on or before 31 December 2008). The consent form for the minor's legal guardian is available in the registration system in the six official languages.

Q66.q: We would like to know whether minors can stay in the same accommodation as their chaperones or parents, whether they will be separated from the group and allocated to separate accommodation, and who is responsible for minors if they cannot stay with their chaperones.
Q66.a: Minor pilgrims will be allocated to the same accommodation as their parents or adult chaperone (the person named as chaperone in the written letter of delegation with the consent of the parent or legal guardian). When accompanied by an adult chaperone who is not a parent, we plan to physically separate the sleeping areas within the same accommodation. However, please understand that various approaches may be applied to accommodation for minors depending on each country's safeguarding regulations and the safety situation on site, and that it is difficult to set a single policy that applies uniformly to every case. The Local Organising Committee presents the WYD Seoul 2027 Safeguarding Guidelines for minors while respecting the safeguarding guidelines and standards of each country's Bishops' Conference. However, the decision on which accommodation arrangement to choose under those standards, and the responsibility that follows, rests with each pilgrim group.

Q67.q: Under Scottish safeguarding rules, religious and clergy leaders may not stay in the same accommodation as young people. Will separate spaces be provided for them? What about toilets?
Q67.a: No separate spaces have been prepared for religious and clergy leaders. If you make a separate request after registering, we will do our best to accommodate it. However, please understand that this may be difficult to provide depending on the conditions of the accommodation.

Q68.q: If a minor needs hospital treatment or admission in an emergency, can the group leader accompany them and receive information about their medical condition and treatment? Also, are guardian consent and the sharing of medical information for this purpose included in the minor registration form?
Q68.a: The current minor registration procedure does not include separate items on medical consent or the sharing of medical information for adult chaperones or group leaders. However, an adult chaperone who has received a written letter of delegation and consent from the parent or legal guardian can be regarded as having comprehensive chaperoning rights over the minor. We are considering including guardian consent for emergency treatment and the sharing of medical information in the 'Guidelines for the Protection of Minors and Vulnerable Adults', which are currently being reviewed and revised, and we will announce the detailed procedure once it is confirmed.

Q69.q: Is there a special package for minors or children accompanied by their parents (a special family package)? If so, how is accommodation allocated? Also, can children under 14 take part if accompanied by one of their parents?
Q69.a: There is no separate special family package for minors or children accompanied by their parents. Children under 14 can also take part if accompanied by at least one parent or by an adult chaperone delegated by their legal guardian. However, packages including accommodation provided by the Local Organising Committee can only be applied for by participants born on or before 31 July 2013. The accommodation provided by the Local Organising Committee consists mainly of shared facilities such as schools and public buildings, and homestays. Considering this accommodation environment and the conditions for hosting a large number of pilgrims, families taking part with children under 14 are asked to register for a package without accommodation and to arrange suitable accommodation for their family themselves.

Q70.q: In a group registration system without individual registration, how is each pilgrim's agreement to and signature of the safeguarding policy and Code of Conduct obtained? Also, will the relevant guidelines be provided before the registration system opens, and will separate training be offered for pilgrims?
Q70.a: In the registration system, depending on the type of participation, pilgrim group leaders, clergy (priests and deacons), bishops, volunteers, Catholic Cultural Fair participants, Youth Festival participants, journalists and others are required to agree to and sign the safeguarding policy and Code of Conduct. Individual pilgrims must also agree to and sign the policy and Code of Conduct through the pilgrim app. The safeguarding guidelines and Code of Conduct are currently being reviewed and revised, and the final versions will be shared in early 2027 through the registration system, the official website and the Bishops' Conferences, among others. Training materials will also be provided to help pilgrims understand and comply with the safeguarding policy and Code of Conduct.

Q71.q: We would like to know whether pilgrims with disabilities are allocated separate accommodation depending on the type of disability or support needed, and whether they can receive support from dedicated staff from arrival in Korea until departure.
Q71.a: As a rule, pilgrims with disabilities also travel with their diocese, but they can be allocated to separate accommodation if they wish. It is preferable for them to have a companion within the group from arrival in Korea until departure, but if not, we are also considering assigning a volunteer.

Q72.q: Can pilgrims with disabilities stay and take part in events with their own group, such as their diocesan or Bishops' Conference delegation, while receiving the accessibility and mobility support they need?
Q72.a: Pilgrims with disabilities will be able to stay with their own group, such as their diocese or Bishops' Conference delegation, while receiving the accessibility and mobility support they need. Details of the support will be announced later through the app or the website.

Q73.q: What is the registration procedure for pilgrims with disabilities? Please also let us know whether registering a guardian or companion is mandatory and, if necessary, how to register a pilgrim with a disability together with their companion.
Q73.a: During registration, there is a checklist item asking whether you are accompanying a pilgrim with a disability. If so, please tick it. Registering a companion is not mandatory; if there is a companion, please register the companion as a pilgrim too and enter the companion's name and contact details in the notes field.

Q74.q: Where do we collect pilgrim kits, cards, etc.? Where are the check-in and collection points for groups with accommodation and groups without accommodation?
Q74.a: Groups registered for a package with accommodation will check in at their allocated parish and collect their pilgrim kits, cards, etc. there. The Local Organising Committee will deliver these items to each parish in advance. Groups registered for a package without accommodation will check in at the Pilgrim Centre and collect their pilgrim kits, cards, etc. there. Participants registering on site can also collect these items at the Pilgrim Centre after completing the registration procedure.

Q75.q: What is in the pilgrim kit?
Q75.a: It is expected to include a backpack (bag), a T-shirt, a hat, a water bottle, a (folding) fan, a sports towel and a rosary (bracelet), but some items may change.

Q76.q: How can pilgrims without a smartphone access the information and services needed for check-in and participation in events, and how will they receive the cards and items they need, such as the meal card?
Q76.a: The group leaders must activate the cards and provide any additional information. At check-in, the group leader receives the kits, including the prepaid cards, on behalf of the group and distributes them to the members.

Q77.q: Do priests and deacons check in with their group, or must they check in at a separate designated place? We would like to know whether the group leader can verify the identity of priests and deacons and collect clergy items such as stoles on their behalf, or whether they must come in person.
Q77.a:
Priests and deacons registered for a package with accommodation can check in with their group at the allocated parish. However, since the check-in staff verify the identity of priests and deacons in person before issuing credentials and kits, the group leader cannot verify their identity or collect these items on their behalf. Priests and deacons registered for a package without accommodation must go in person to the dedicated check-in point for priests and deacons at the Pilgrim Centre for identity verification and collection of items.
We are considering having stoles and vestments collected in person at the closing Mass, and the specific collection procedure will be announced once confirmed.

Q78.q: For groups without accommodation, can the group leader check in and collect items at the Pilgrim Centre on behalf of the group without bringing all the pilgrims?
Q78.a: Yes. For groups registered for a package without accommodation, the group leader can visit the Pilgrim Centre on behalf of the group and carry out group check-in and item collection without all participants being present. However, priests and deacons in the group must go in person to the dedicated check-in point for priests and deacons at the Pilgrim Centre and complete a separate check-in procedure.

Q79.q: What are the daily opening hours of the Pilgrim Centre?
Q79.a: The Pilgrim Centre, where on-site registration and check-in for groups with packages without accommodation will take place, is scheduled to operate from 25 July, when check-in for short-term volunteers begins, until 8 August. More detailed operating plans will be announced later.

Q80.q: Will public Wi-Fi be provided at accommodation and main event venues during WYD for smooth internet use, such as using the pilgrim app? Will a communications environment be in place that remains stable even when large numbers of pilgrims connect at the same time?
Q80.a: Many public Wi-Fi hotspots are installed throughout Seoul. The Local Organising Committee is cooperating in various areas with the Seoul Metropolitan Government and related companies and institutions for the convenience and safety of pilgrims.

Q81.q: Can we also be informed about how the pilgrimage routes approved by the Holy See operate, how to take part, and the procedure for issuing a pilgrimage confirmation or certificate?
Q81.a:
The pilgrimage routes approved by the Holy See can be visited and walked freely at any time without a separate application. The routes consist of 24 sites in total and three courses (Course 1: The Way of the Word / Course 2: The Way of Life / Course 3: The Way of Unity).
If you visit all three museums included in the WYD-only programme 'Pilgrimage Route with Museums', you can download a certificate of completion. You can visit during museum opening hours without prior application; tour the museum with Bluetooth turned on on your smartphone and the pilgrim app running. The verification device in the museum connects with your phone, and your visit is verified automatically in the pilgrim app. When you have visited all three designated museums, a message confirming that verification is complete will appear. Tap the 'Download certificate of completion' button at the bottom of the screen to receive your certificate.

Q82.q: We would like to know whether group leaders and subgroup leaders can use both their own pilgrim functions and their leader functions within the same app. In other words, can they switch between their own screen and the leader screen?
Q82.a:
This is not possible.
Web membership -> participation verification (group code) -> leader verification can only be used consistently with one account. If you want to use N accounts, you need to register N web memberships from the start. However, some information stored locally on the phone to make offline use of the app smoother may be excluded (favourites, certificates of completion, etc.).

Q83.q: Does each pilgrim receive a personal account and login details and activate the app themselves?
Q83.a:
Each person signs up for web membership freely.
For the group code, you can receive additional verification by entering the group information shared by your leader.

Q84.q: If one email is used for one account, should the email and password be shared within the group to log in, or does each participant log in with their own account even if they are entered as several items in the same group in the app?
Q84.a: An account is personal information, so each person must sign up individually. This is separate from group code verification.

Q85.q: Does the app require an internet connection? If so, will Wi-Fi be provided, or do pilgrims need to buy a SIM card or eSIM?
Q85.a: Pilgrims can use the app with public Wi-Fi and their own mobile data. However, the app is designed so that minimal functions remain available even offline (e.g. event information). Pilgrims must purchase and use their own SIM card or eSIM.

Q86.q: Does the pilgrim app provide functions such as multilingual translation or a chatbot for enquiries? For example, is there a function to translate text by taking a photo or to translate conversations by voice?
Q86.a: The pilgrim app is available in six languages. No separate translation or interpretation functions are provided.

Q87.q: Can the pilgrim app provide, or give real-time guidance on, local information that pilgrims need, such as the location and capacity of nearby restaurants? When using restaurants near pilgrimage sites, many teams may arrive at once, so people may wander around looking for a restaurant and miss mealtime, or be unable to eat because of an unexpected menu.
Q87.a: The pilgrim app does not provide current information on all restaurants.

Q88.q: From when can the pilgrim app be downloaded and used, and does it support both iOS and Android? Also, can the main functions of the app be used offline when the internet connection is poor?
Q88.a: The app is currently in service. Basic information is updated online at regular intervals so that it can also be used offline, but new information can only be retrieved online.

Q89.q: Is live interpretation of the main events also available in the pilgrim app, or only via radio frequency?
Q89.a: The pilgrim app does not provide a live interpretation function.

Q90.q: What information must be entered by group leaders and by pilgrims respectively, and how is information such as passport details, T-shirt size and allergies registered? Please also explain the functions of the group leader dashboard.
Q90.a:
Advance information can only be entered by the group leader. Pilgrims cannot enter advance information.
A verified group leader, as the group's representative, is given permission to enter advance information and to activate and request reissue of the group members' prepaid cards.

Q91.q: What personal information is entered in the app and when, and is information such as T-shirt size and allergies entered by pilgrims themselves or managed by the group leader? Please also let us know whether this information can be entered and managed on the website, and what measures are in place for personal data protection and app security.
Q91.a: As standard, a verification code for web membership is sent to the member's own email address. Advance information is entered only by the group leader. Personal information applies only to the basic web membership, and the terms, which have been legally reviewed, are provided and consent is obtained when signing up.

Q92.q: Will a step-by-step user guide or a trial environment be provided on the official site so that participants can get familiar with the pilgrim app in advance?
Q92.a: The app is currently in service, and an advance guide to the app will be provided.

Q93.q: Can the WYD pilgrim transport card be added to and used in mobile wallets such as Apple Pay, Google Pay or Samsung Pay?
Q93.a: The pilgrim card is issued as a physical card that combines a transport card and a payment card. This physical card does not support NFC linking.

Q94.q: After WYD, if there is a balance of, say, about 100 dollars left on the prepaid meal card, can it be refunded? If so, is the refund in won or in dollars? Or could you at least allow it to be donated to the Solidarity Fund?
Q94.a: If the meal allowance topped up daily by the Local Organising Committee is not fully used on the day, the balance is carried over and can be used until the end date of the registered package. Unused balances are not refunded after the event. We are discussing donating unused balances as part of the participation contribution. Further details will be provided later.

Q95.q: Is the prepaid meal card a physical card or a digital one? During the Rome Jubilee, there were major problems with the app, and some groups did not receive all their meals.
Q95.a: The prepaid meal card is a physical card. The pilgrim app does not provide a payment function; you can check your usage history and balance in it.

Q96.q: During WYD, are meals chosen freely at restaurants, convenience stores, etc. using the prepaid meal card, or are separate meal tents or packed meals also provided? Do the participating restaurants and convenience stores include places serving food from various cultures?
Q96.a: Breakfast will be provided collectively at the accommodation, and lunch and dinner will be available freely at designated restaurants using the prepaid meal card. Details such as the participating restaurants, menus and how the meal card will operate are currently under discussion.

Q97.q: Is an NFC function on the phone required to use the prepaid meal card?
Q97.a: No. The physical card received at check-in can be activated and linked to your phone for use. An NFC function is not required.

Q98.q: If a pilgrim card is lost, can only the second leader issue/request a new card, or can the first leader also do so?
Q98.a: All app-related permissions belong to the second leader only. Because, as a matter of policy, a person can be both a Subgroup leader and the first leader, the second leader is the only unique leader account, which is why this decision was made.

Q99.q: Is there a dedicated contact point or person at the Local Organising Committee to coordinate continental, regional and national gatherings during WYD, and will venues be provided for these gatherings? Or must the organising bodies arrange venues themselves?
Q99.a: Please send proposals for continental or national gatherings to the International Department (international@wydseoul.org). You will receive detailed guidance on event operations and practical matters.

Q100.q: Will the Local Organising Committee provide an official programme and prayer materials so that countries and young people who cannot attend WYD in person can take part through their own events and vigils in their dioceses or parishes?
Q100.a: The Local Organising Committee is planning and preparing various ways for pilgrims who cannot be present on site for various reasons. We will announce the format and method of participation as soon as they are confirmed.
